missions.name: Landsat 1
missions.short: The first mission proved that systematic multispectral land imaging from space could become a durable public utility.
missions.summary: Originally launched as the Earth Resources Technology Satellite, Landsat 1 started the world's longest continuous space-based record of land observations and validated the scientific value of multispectral Earth imaging.
missions.highlight: The key shift was cultural as much as technical: Landsat 1 helped move Earth observation from experimental imagery toward repeatable, decision-grade monitoring.

missions.name: Landsat 2
missions.short: Strengthened the case for repeated seasonal land imaging and global archive building.
missions.summary: Landsat 2 expanded the early program and reinforced the value of MSS data for resource monitoring, especially where repeated wide-area observations were more useful than isolated snapshots.
missions.highlight: It helped establish that continuity and seasonal revisits mattered just as much as any single image.

missions.name: Landsat 3
missions.short: Extended the MSS record and briefly introduced a thermal capability before sensor failure.
missions.summary: Landsat 3 preserved continuity while experimenting with added spectral capability, including an early thermal band that unfortunately failed shortly after deployment.
missions.highlight: Even partial improvements mattered because the program was still defining what the long-term Landsat template should become.

missions.name: Landsat 4
missions.short: Marked the shift into the Thematic Mapper era with much stronger spectral and spatial performance.
missions.summary: Landsat 4 introduced the Thematic Mapper, a major capability step that improved spatial resolution and spectral richness, setting the standard for modern moderate-resolution land monitoring.
missions.highlight: This is one of the most important technical turning points in the program because TM made many contemporary Landsat applications possible.

missions.name: Landsat 5
missions.short: Delivered one of the longest and most influential Earth-observation records ever collected.
missions.summary: Landsat 5 far exceeded its design life and became a workhorse for land-change analysis worldwide, generating a vast share of the historical baseline used in modern environmental science.
missions.highlight: Its extraordinary longevity is one reason the Landsat archive is so powerful for decadal comparisons.

missions.name: Landsat 6
missions.short: Did not reach orbit, but its intended instrument path pointed toward the next generation.
missions.summary: Landsat 6 failed to achieve orbit after launch, creating a significant continuity challenge, but its planned Enhanced Thematic Mapper configuration foreshadowed later system evolution.
missions.highlight: It is a reminder that continuity in Earth observation depends on resilience in both policy and hardware.

missions.name: Landsat 7
missions.resolution: 15 m pan, 30 m multispectral, 60 m thermal
missions.short: A landmark archive mission whose science acquisitions ended January 19, 2024 and whose spacecraft was decommissioned June 4, 2025.
missions.summary: Landsat 7 sustained the archive deep into the digital and open-data era. Even after the 2003 scan line corrector anomaly, it remained a vital source for long time-series analysis and historical continuity.
missions.highlight: The mission's official end matters: as of June 4, 2025, Landsat 7 is no longer an active imaging asset, but its archive remains essential.

missions.name: Landsat 8
missions.resolution: 15 m pan, 30 m VNIR/SWIR, 100 m thermal
missions.short: Introduced the modern OLI/TIRS architecture and still anchors today's operational record.
missions.summary: Landsat 8 modernized the program with pushbroom imaging, improved radiometry, coastal aerosol and cirrus bands, and strong continuity with previous mission products.
missions.highlight: If you are building present-day Landsat workflows, Landsat 8 remains part of the core operational pair with Landsat 9.

missions.name: Landsat 9
missions.resolution: 15 m pan, 30 m VNIR/SWIR, 100 m thermal
missions.short: The newest Landsat in orbit, extending continuity with strong calibration and 14-bit radiometric precision.
missions.summary: Landsat 9 is the first mission under the Sustainable Land Imaging Program and continues the core Landsat record with improved radiometric precision, high daily scene throughput, and tight continuity with Landsat 8.
missions.highlight: NASA states Landsat 9 collects around 740 scenes per day, nearly double its original minimum daily requirement.
